strengths: The method and algorithms are technically sound, with reasonable insights and solutions.
The writing is good and also the mathematics are true.
The problem of dimensionality reduction for data on a manifold is well motivated, and the proposed method closes the gap between PPCA and data on manifolds.
The proposed extension PPCA is innovative and well explained.
The mathematical derivation of the EM-algorithm is concise and understandable, and the empirical experiments show promising results.
weaknesses: Comparison with other nonlinear PPCA methods is not provided.
The reason for the assumption of nonlinear manifold terms in the PPCA extension is not clear.

Experiments on real data are not clear; the method should be evaluated on more general data such as well-known image data sets, or at least mention the class of real data where it works well compared to PPCA, making the importance and quality of the proposed method unclear.
The complexity of the proposed method should be reported.

The simulated data seems favorable for PGPCA compared to PPCA; it is unclear how PGPCA performs on data generated from linear subspaces or manifolds close to linear, and experiments should be included to assess performance in such scenarios.

PGPCA is only compared to PPCA and not to other potentially stronger baseline methods; comparisons with manifold learning methods such as Isomap, Laplacian Eigenmaps, or diffusion maps are missing, making it unclear if PGPCA offers any advantage over existing methods.

The evaluation on real data is rather limited, using only brain signals of two mice; more real-world datasets are needed to demonstrate general applicability and to support strong claims about the practical relevance of PGPCA.
